title: Precision Cut Lung Slices as Ex Vivo Human Lung Tissue Model of Cellular Senescence
author: Sadiya Shaikh
materials: Carefully retrieve, thaw and culture the PCLS
Supernatant Collection for Luminex or Similar Assay
Homogenize using pellet pestle or motorized homogenizer.
Assess expression of senescence and immune-related transcripts.
Isolation for single cell RNA sequencing
PCLS Preservation and Preparation for Immunohistochemistry.
o Quantify cytokines using provided standard curves.
o Analyze using Luminex reader FLEXMAP 3D.
o Run samples and standards in technical duplicates.

steps.title: Initial PCLS Culture and Stabilization
steps.instruction: Transfer individual PCLS into wells of a 6-well Tissue Culture plate containing 5 ml pre-warmed culture medium (DMEM+10%FBS+1% Antibiotic/Antimycotic).

substeps.instruction: Wash PCLS 3 times in 5 ml Culture Media.
Transfer PCLS into a 24-well Tissue Culture plate with 1 ml fresh media.
Incubate at 37°C with 5% CO₂ for approximately 24 hours to allow slices to stabilize.

steps.title: Ionizing Radiation Treatment
steps.instruction: Expose PCLS to a defined dose of ionizing radiation using a Cesium-137 irradiator.

substeps.instruction: Transfer sealed plates to the irradiation facility in a sterile container or biosafety-approved transport method, maintaining room temperature and minimizing delays.
Include control plates in the transport to control for temperature changes.
Place the plate in the Cesium-137 irradiator chamber (certified personnel required).
Deliver a defined dose of ionizing radiation (commonly 5 Gy or 10 Gy; 10 Gy was used in the described experiment), ensuring uniform exposure across the plate.
Immediately return PCLS to a 37°C, 5% CO₂ incubator.

steps.title: Post-Irradiation Recovery
steps.instruction: Allow the tissue to recover in the incubator before starting treatment.

substeps.instruction: Recover for 4–6 hours (standard) or optionally extend to 24 hours to assess delayed transcriptional or secretory responses.

steps.title: Administration of Senotherapeutics
steps.instruction: Administer senescence inducers, senolytics, or senomorphics to the PCLS by adding drugs directly to the culture medium to achieve final concentrations.

substeps.instruction: Include DMSO or other carrier-treated wells as vehicle controls.
Use single agents or combination treatments as per experimental design.
Example: For Fisetin (Fisher Scientific, AC119150010), reconstitute in DMSO and add to a final concentration of 20 µM 48 hours after irradiation.
Incubate treated PCLS at 37°C, 5% CO₂ in medium +/- at air-liquid interface.
For long-term senescence studies, culture for 7 days, refreshing media every 2 days to maintain nutrient levels.

steps.title: Supernatant Collection for Luminex Analysis
steps.instruction: Collect culture supernatants for analysis of SASP factors.

substeps.instruction: Carefully transfer ~400 µL of supernatant from each well into labeled low-binding tubes.
Centrifuge briefly (e.g., 5 min at 500 x g) to remove debris.
Aliquot and freeze at –80°C.
When analyzing, thaw supernatants on ice and dilute if necessary; set up the Luminex plate according to kit instructions.

steps.title: RNA Isolation and NanoString Analysis
steps.instruction: Extract RNA from PCLS and perform NanoString nCounter assay.

substeps.instruction: Transfer each PCLS into a 1.5 mL tube with 350 µL RLT buffer or Trizol.
Isolate RNA using a chosen RNA kit and elute in 15–30 µL nuclease-free water.
Measure RNA concentration and integrity using Nanodrop/Qubit and Bioanalyzer or TapeStation.
If using frozen samples: Remove vial from liqN2, keep on dry ice, and thaw quickly by holding between fingers or briefly in a 37°C water bath.
Hybridize 50–100 ng of purified RNA with NanoString Reporter and Capture probes for 16 hours at 65°C.
Load reactions into the NanoString Prep Station for purification and immobilization.
Scan samples using the nCounter Digital Analyzer and analyze data using nSolver software.

steps.title: Tissue Fixation and Dehydration
steps.instruction: Fix and prepare PCLS sections for histology.

substeps.instruction: Transfer a PCLS section flat onto a biopsy foam pad inside a cassette, sandwich with another foam pad, and close the lid.
Place cassettes in 10% NBF at 4°C overnight (up to 24 hours).
Rinse cassettes for 20 minutes in 1x PBS with agitation on a rotating platform at room temperature.
Perform successive 20-minute agitations in 30% EtOH, 50% EtOH, and 70% EtOH.
Store cassettes in 70% EtOH at 4°C overnight.

steps.title: Paraffin Embedding
steps.instruction: Process tissue through a VIP processor and embed in paraffin.

substeps.instruction: Place cassettes in the VIP processor's retort and run the 'SHORT' program: 70% EtOH (15 min, 40°C), 80% EtOH (15 min, 40°C), 95% EtOH (2x 15 min, 40°C), 100% EtOH (15 min and 20 min, 40°C), Xylene (2x 20 min, 40°C), and Paraffin (15 min, 30 min, 15 min, all at 60°C).
Transfer tissue from cassettes into metal embedding molds, ensuring the tissue remains flat.
Cool on a cold plate until solid, then store blocks at room temperature.

steps.title: Sectioning and Slide Preparation
steps.instruction: Section the paraffin blocks for imaging or staining.

substeps.instruction: Fill a hot water bath with DEPC treated water and set to 45°C.
Trim the block at 10 µm using a microtome until tissue is exposed.
Place the block on ice for 10 minutes.
Section the block at 5 µm (or 4 µm) thickness to create a ribbon.
Float the ribbon on the hot water bath and pick up sections onto TruBond 380 Adhesive Microscope Slides in serial order.
Dry slides upright overnight, then store at room temperature for H&E or CODEX staining.

steps.title: Multiplexed Immunofluorescence (MxIF) Imaging
steps.instruction: Perform MxIF analysis on FFPE PCLS sections.

substeps.instruction: Image slides using a Phenocycler Imaging System following the CODEX MxIF Protocol.
